findings.fix: Remove this paragraph from the form body and show a thank-you message only after successful submission.
findings.location: `row-phone` div, inside the phone number field
findings.violation: A post-submission thank-you message is hard-coded into the middle of the form, before the user has submitted anything.

findings.fix: Raise the minimum (e.g. 8+ characters), and add visible helper text near the field describing the requirement.
findings.violation: A 6-character minimum with no complexity requirement is a weak password policy, and no visible hint tells the user any requirement exists.

findings.fix: Make this field optional, or remove it if it isn't actually needed for individual membership.
findings.violation: "Company website" is marked required on what appears to be an individual membership signup, which will block anyone without a company site from completing the form.

findings.fix: Add `pattern="\d{8}"` plus `minlength="8" maxlength="8"`, and move the instruction into persistent helper text rather than relying on the placeholder alone.
findings.violation: The 8-digit requirement is communicated only via placeholder text (which disappears once the user types) and isn't enforced by any validation attribute.

findings.evidence: `<label id="acctnum-label" for="acctnum-input">Account number</label>` required on an account-creation form
findings.fix: Remove this field, or clarify what it refers to (e.g. an existing loyalty/customer number) and make it optional.
findings.violation: Requiring an "account number" on a form whose purpose is to create the account is contradictory - the user doesn't have one yet.

findings.fix: Pick one representation of name and remove the other.
findings.violation: The form collects the user's name twice in two different, potentially inconsistent formats (one combined field, one split pair).

findings.evidence: Two `<label>`/`<input>` pairs (`given-input`, `family-input`) inside a single row div, unlike every other row which holds exactly one field
findings.fix: Split into two separate row divs (e.g. `row-given`, `row-family`) matching the pattern used elsewhere.
findings.violation: This breaks the one-field-per-row convention used everywhere else in the form, making the markup structurally inconsistent.

findings.fix: Apply a consistent minimum font-size (via a shared stylesheet rule, not scattered inline styles) to all text inputs.
findings.violation: This looks like a fix for the mobile-Safari auto-zoom bug (inputs under 16px trigger zoom on focus), but it's applied to only one field, leaving every other text input susceptible to the same issue.

findings.fix: Increase padding/font-size to meet at least a 24x24px (ideally 44x44px) touch target.
findings.violation: This tap target is far below accessible minimum size guidelines (effectively a few pixels), making it very hard to tap reliably, especially on touch devices.

findings.evidence: `<button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" ...>View details</button>` with no `<script>` anywhere in the document
findings.fix: Either add the script that gives this button a function, or remove it until that logic exists.
findings.violation: The button has no attached behavior since the document contains no JavaScript at all, so it is currently a dead control.

findings.evidence: Only `street_address` and `postal_code` fields exist; no city, state/region, or country field
findings.fix: Add city and state/region (and country, if international) fields alongside street address and postal code.
findings.violation: The address collected is incomplete for shipping purposes, yet the form also asks for a "Preferred shipping speed" (`row-shipspeed`), implying physical shipment.

findings.fix: Add explicit `action` and `method` attributes, or confirm and document the JS handler that intercepts submission.
findings.violation: Without `action`/`method`, the form's submission destination and HTTP method are undefined, so submit behavior depends entirely on unseen JS.

findings.evidence: `<button id="submit-btn" type="submit">Create account</button>` immediately followed by `<button id="reset-btn" type="reset">Clear form</button>`
findings.fix: Remove the reset button, or visually separate/de-emphasize it and add a confirmation step before clearing.
findings.violation: Placing a reset button directly next to the submit button risks accidental full data loss from a single misclick after filling out a long form.

findings.fix: Replace with a `<select>` of defined time ranges or an `<input type="time">`/structured control.
findings.violation: Using a free-text field for "Preferred contact time" invites inconsistent, unparseable values (e.g. "morning" vs "9am" vs "AM").

findings.evidence: Street address appears right after the password field, while postal code appears much later, separated by phone, phone2, website, membership number, and account number
findings.fix: Move `row-postal` to immediately follow `row-street` (and add city/state fields there too) so address information is grouped together.
findings.location: Field order across the form (`row-street` vs `row-postal`)
findings.violation: Splitting the two address-related fields apart with several unrelated fields in between makes the form's logical grouping confusing to fill out.
